technical.summary: BRK-B shows short-term bullish momentum with strong price action (new highs, three white soldiers) and trend confirmation, but lacks medium-term uptrend alignment and overbought conditions limit upside potential.

fundamental.summary: No actionable fundamental or smart money signals detected; insider/institutional activity absent, government contracts and lobbying data unavailable, and earnings in 71 days present timing risk.

sentiment.summary: Extreme fear (11/100) presents contrarian buy opportunity; no congressional activity or recent news sentiment to confirm or contradict setup.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds with VIX in crisis territory (359.36), flat yield curve signalling recession risk, and elevated credit stress create highly unfavourable conditions for equities despite 71-day earnings buffer.

debate.key_bull_argument: Three white soldiers + DC10 new high + supertrend bullish provide short-term momentum confirmation, and extreme fear (11/100) presents classic contrarian buy setup near support at 310.86.
debate.key_bear_argument: Macro environment is in crisis (VIX 359.36, inverted yield curve, high credit spreads), price fails to hold above 50-SMA/EMA-50, overbought oscillators limit upside, and earnings in 71 days create event risk in unfavourable conditions.

decision.entry_rationale: Short-term technicals (three white soldiers, DC10 new high) show momentum, and extreme fear presents contrarian opportunity. However, macro crisis conditions, overbought oscillators, and lack of medium-term trend confirmation make risk/reward unfavourable.
decision.primary_risk: VIX in crisis territory (359.36) with inverted yield curve and elevated credit spreads create systemic headwinds that can reverse short-term momentum sharply; earnings in 71 days add event risk.
decision.agent_agreement: moderate — technicals bullish but fundamentals, sentiment, and risk all warn against entry; macro environment overrides short-term signals
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding BRK-B with 55 existing Financials positions (18.8% of portfolio); concentration risk and sector saturation argue against adding exposure.
